The fourth preview of CoSky 8.0. There is still **no compatibility promise**: the API, the wire format and the Redis keys may change before the beta, and nothing here is ready for real traffic. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

This one fixes 37 issues a review of `8.0.0-alpha.3` found, and a few more found while fixing them.

## Changed

- **Default instance names are `<service>_<host>_<port>`.** Joining with `-`, which services and hosts may hold, gave `billing-api` on `node` and `billing` on `api-node` the same name, so the second could not register. A name longer than 253 characters keeps its port and ends in a digest of the whole name.
- **Each Spring application has its own client.** Applications in one JVM no longer share one: each reports under its own `spring.application.name`, and closing one leaves the others' instances alone. A start that fails while loading configuration closes its client.
- **Deleting a namespace marks it first.** `namespace.terminating` is `true` while a deletion is under way, and a write to the Namespace gets `404`. A namespace created again goes on counting revisions instead of starting at 1, so an `If-Match` kept from before the deletion no longer matches anything in it.
- **A lease TTL the protocol does not take is refused** when the client is built: whole seconds from 5 to 300. It used to become the server's default of 30 seconds.
- **History page tokens have a new form**, and those of earlier alphas are refused. A rollback that changes nothing sends no ETag, like any write that changes nothing.
- **Snapshot files are named by a digest**, so that every legal Config name fits in a file name.

## Fixed

- **Server and store**
  - A later page of a list waits for the first page's revision on a replica that is behind, rather than ending early.
  - An archive import no longer undoes labels or a format written elsewhere meanwhile.
  - Expired leases with a long TTL no longer hold back short ones that are ready to be reaped.
  - Versions written while a history is paged no longer push out older ones.
  - Closing a store releases its Redis connections and client.
- **Client and starter**
  - A view no longer goes back to an older value after a snapshot that held a newer one.
  - A registration made while the server was away goes out once it is back. One the server then refuses gives way to the registration it would have replaced, and putting back a lost instance leaves an operator's drain of another alone.
  - A renewal stream that answers nothing is opened again, rather than waited on until the lease runs out.
  - A snapshot holds its view with its own position, and an earlier write never replaces a later one.
  - A refresh that fails on one import still clears a deleted Config the next time.
  - Spring gets bracketed URIs for IPv6 instances.
  - Closing the client during an endpoint switch leaves no channel open, and a watch added during a reconnect is created once.
- **Dashboard**
  - The namespace list, expanded services and expanded histories keep up with changes.
  - The drawer closes with its page, and a save that ends late closes only its own drawer.
  - The topology follows the overview's refresh, keeps every dependency, keeps long names inside their nodes, and no longer overlaps crowded layers.
  - The config diff releases its editor models, and says why when it cannot read the current version.
- **Migration:** a resumed `--history` run skips no version, also when a content came back or an old version was too large for 8.0.
- **Image:** native access is enabled for Netty's epoll transport, which sets the TCP user timeout, and JDK 25's warnings at start are gone.

## Upgrading from an earlier alpha

- Applications register under their new default names. During a rolling upgrade both names show until the old processes stop; one that does not stop cleanly is removed when its lease expires, about 40 seconds later.
- Snapshots saved by earlier alphas are not found: an application starts as without one. The old files under `~/.cosky` can be deleted.
- History page tokens issued before the upgrade are refused; list from the first page.
- Redis data needs nothing.

## Verified since alpha.3

- 20,000 connections: a propagation p99 of 154 to 189 ms in 4 runs. The 5.8-second tail seen before came from the load generator, not the server.
- `cosky-migrate` on data a 6.2.0 server wrote.
- `kubectl drain` on a k3s cluster of four nodes, one node after another and two at once, with no failed write, read or registration.

## Known limits

- **Not yet tried:** Redis Cluster at this scale, or a real network between the parts. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
